sections.title: Sound of esse
paragraphs: The letter is named (esse) /ˈɛsi/. Its main sound appears in (sol) /ˈsɔɫ/, which means sun. This letter has four different sounds.

sections.title: How to say esse
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue near the tooth ridge. Push air through without voice. Voiceless means your throat does not shake. For the second sound, make the same hissing noise, but add your voice. For the third sound, raise your tongue blade further back. Blow air through with no voice. For the fourth sound, keep that rear tongue position and add voice. Feel your throat vibrate.

sections.title: Spelling rules for esse
paragraphs: At the start of a word, it sounds as in (sapo) /ˈsa.pu/. Doubled between vowels, it makes that same sound, as in (passo) /ˈpa.su/. Single between vowels, it sounds as in (casa) /ˈka.zɐ/. At the end of a syllable before a pause, it sounds as in (português) /puɾ.tuˈɡeʃ/. Before another consonant that has no voice, it also makes that sound, as in (festa) /ˈfɛʃ.tɐ/. Before a voiced consonant, it sounds as in (mesmo) /ˈmeʒ.mu/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with esse
paragraphs: At the end of a word, do not use the hissing sound from English bus. In (português) /puɾ.tuˈɡeʃ/, say the quiet sh sound from English ship instead. Before a voiced consonant, avoid the buzzing sound from English zoom. In (mesmo) /ˈmeʒ.mu/, make the soft sound from the middle of English measure.
